verdict.rationale: DBOS ships dedicated docs for agent workloads (ai-quickstart, hitl, debugging) describing exactly this pattern: LLM/tool calls as durable steps that checkpoint to Postgres and recover after crashes, restarts, or long human-in-the-loop waits, plus fork/replay for debugging and OpenAI Agents SDK drop-in integration (DBOSRunner). Community posts corroborate the underlying checkpointing/recovery mechanism (log-and-replay steps, exactly-once semantics) though one HN critique notes durability is bounded by Postgres's own replication guarantees rather than being stronger. Missing for 10: independent hands-on case study specifically of an LLM agent loop (not just generic workflows) surviving a crash, and no benchmark/evidence on step-level cost for long LLM tool-call chains.
